interpretationConstraints: Only ordinary timing captures are used for timing comparisons; full Compose tracing supplies mechanism evidence separately.
Per-iteration frame percentiles are linear interpolation of the raw Macrobenchmark sampledMetrics arrays, not pooled frame samples.
CPU is clipped to actual measureBlock duration, which can exceed the requested 4000ms due to gesture/check overhead; CPU and composition rates are normalized.
FrameTimeline diagnostic rows are fully contained in measureBlock. Macrobenchmark raw frame arrays include its boundary-frame selection and can have a different cardinality.
Phase comparison separates frames starting before vs after the first positive stream-update counter (about135–158ms), inside measureBlock. It does not replace official full raw metrics.

Macrobenchmark raw arrays also include post-measureBlock stop-transition frames in these archives: restoring the completed rich answer produced extra tails. Exact matching overruns identify those rows in boundaryFrames.

Streaming is synthetic word-level text updates at a requested 100ms period, with no concurrent native inference. Activation replaces a completed answer with a streaming prefix and changes composer controls.
Composition calls have no row IDs and cannot conclusively assign individual calls to visible vs prefetched rows. Inclusive wall/CPU timings are nested and must not be added.
Refresh validation records active display mode at endpoints and separate callback/surface cadence. Frame deadline budget is not treated as physical refresh rate.
Google process CPU is observed concurrent work, not causal proof of a frame delay. System/SurfaceFlinger CPU also contains normal benchmark rendering work.
Three timing iterations per condition are an exploratory pilot, not evidence of a small statistically reliable latency improvement.
experiment: Active-row StreamingState isolation, fixture v3, Pixel 9, 2026-10-24

decision.reason: Equivalent rendering branches with a proven reduction in unused row-wrapper composition; absolute CPU saving is very small, and timing pilot does not establish an improvement or sustained regression.

candidate120HzProbe.scope: Candidate-only ordinary timing probe; separate rebuilt APK, not an A/B experiment or evidence that row isolation improves120Hz performance.
candidate120HzProbe.refreshSemantics: 120Hz display active mode at endpoints; observed callback median8.34–8.36ms, surface median8.339ms and VsyncPeriod8.333ms. Expected16.6ms duration is a scheduled render deadline budget, not the physical refresh period. Neither cadence median nor negative overrun proves every frame presented without extra latency.

run2QueuedFrames.inputContext: Final MOVE of first swipe; UP is13.508ms after missed-frame start. Nearest synthetic updates are−78.081ms/+22.317ms. Source auto-scroll effect depends on message count/insets/viewport, not token text; no trace evidence establishes an auto-scroll restart.
run2QueuedFrames.prefetchContext: After the missed doFrame, lazy prefetch composition lasts3.465ms, with another1.940ms in the next frame. These overlap rendering; attribution to the fence delay is unproven.
run2QueuedFrames.latencyMethod: Join app surface FrameTimeline tokens to SurfaceFlinger actual display-frame tokens; display end is trace on-screen-update timing, not physical touch-to-photon measurement. Adjacent-frame observations are not a controlled counterfactual.
run2QueuedFrames.conclusion: One additional display interval of queuing is observed. Trace evidence points to a late frame-completion/fence tail during swipe-to-fling, not demonstrated I/O, Google-process scheduling, or token recomposition as its cause. GPU attribution requires another targeted capture.
